subfamily: Manhattan / Brooklyn branch: the Brooklyn Club's rum Manhattan as the Brooklyn Eagle printed it in 1945 (Jamaica rum at 100 proof, Italian vermouth, a dash of Angostura; Hester F17), at 2:1 instead of half-and-half, on Grohusko's 1908 frame (a dash of Amer Picon, a French orange bitter; here an amaro stands in, Oxford pdf 360-361); Codex p. 87: small amaro for part of the vermouth
_status: v3 (Tomás, round 4 step 1). Liquid as v2: the Brooklyn Club's Jamaica rum at 100 proof and its dash of Angostura (Eagle 1945, F17) at 2:1, with Grohusko's amaro slot (CioCiaro). v1 was generic aged rum 40%, no bitters. The club's half-and-half went OUT on acid (0.21). Flamed peel dropped on Wren's ruling (r3): a wide fresh orange peel squeezed high over the top, then dropped in. No maraschino (nuts).
